independence: Cold concise-first review; no authoring conversation, defense, preferred verdict or previous acceptance was used as evidence. Independent first-read recovery retained separately.
proof: review-proof.pdf; two independent settled passes; byte-identical to the supplied author proof; ten physical Letter pages, all embedded subset fonts and no compile diagnostics.

comparison.judgment: First-read recovery identifies two genuinely distinct questions: what received pardon demands and what promised protection means. They complement each other without invented rivalry.

comparison.study_loci: 30-mercy-received: real cancellation, present debtor-creditor, restored liability
comparison.judgment: Preserves argument, not just conclusion: identical pleas and opposite responses, Augustine’s daily debt, and Aquinas’s distinction explain why pardon obliges the heart without falsifying the gift.

comparison.concise_loci: pp. 6–7, debtor/Job comparison and guarded traveler
comparison.judgment: Preserves literal innocence, bounded power, sustaining helper, and Christological fulfillment. Suffering is not treated as evidence of personal guilt; protection is not bodily immunity.

Baptized deliverance, subsequent danger, the girded Passover traveler, sacramental nourishment, and future rest remain connected; reception is not automatic perseverance. Explicit editor dissent remains attached to Chrysostom’s contested glosses.

Preserves Trinity’s equality, personal versus corporate prayer, Bellarmine’s settled peace, Augustine’s final judgment, and Schuster’s present deprivation. These are related but not interchangeable explanations.

comparison.study_loci: Complete study entry graph including appointed texts, history and apparatus; research scope/source bindings
comparison.concise_loci: all six concise components and references
comparison.judgment: No new unsupported source-dependent claim found. Historical translations, adapted chants, editorial constructions, application, biblical context, textually disputed glosses and chronology uncertainty remain marked. The self-contained argument does not require the expansive study; appendix referral supplies further evidence.

source_checks.outcome: Creation and spiritual gifts, the threat intended to prompt supplication, cancellation beyond requested delay, repeated plea/refused mercy, receiver-caused revocation, and endless force of until repayment all support concise pp. 5–6. No inference of fictitious original remission.

Debtor and creditor, the beggar seeking Christ as bread, daily forgiveness after baptism, and loving discipline without inward hatred support pp. 5–6. Modern restitution/protective-boundary applications are identified as applications, not attributed quotations.

source_checks.lines: Complete retained question, especially a. 1 response/reply 1 and a. 2 response
source_checks.outcome: Real past remission remains real; subsequent mortal sin incurs liability and ingratitude rather than numerically restoring the old guilt. The concise distinction preserves the study and Aquinas without neutralizing the patristic warning.

Malicious will differs from bounded permitted power; Job suffers without antecedent crime but with providential ends; the helper simultaneously sustains him. Concise pp. 6–7 preserve innocence and exclude a general diagnosis of sufferers as unforgiving debtors.

source_checks.work: Chrysostom, Ephesians XXII–XXIV and NPNF editorial notes 465, 468
source_checks.outcome: The homily itself recalls Matthew’s forgiven servant in the common-Master argument. Wiles, heavenly prizes/present evil life, Passover girding and spiritual food, all-virtue breastplate, peace/readiness, miraculous faith then confidence in promised goods support pp. 7–8. Editor dissent on high places and evil day survives; Eph. 6:18 remains contextual, beyond the appointed endpoint.

source_checks.work: Augustine, Psalm expositions: NPNF 90 §§1–4; 114 §§1–6; 119 Aleph and Caph
source_checks.outcome: Refuge without divine change, non-compulsory Mosaic authorship, baptized Exodus without automatic perseverance, grace-enabled walking, whole-Christ expectation and martyrs helped through death support the synthesis. Bodily immunity and date prediction are not inferred.
Desire for settled peace and deliverance supports the concise comparison to Augustine’s corporate and eschatological reading; their emphases are not silently equated.
The divine missions imply no inferiority in Son or Spirit. Used as doctrinal illumination of the Preface, not as a claim that Augustine commented on this formulary.

source_checks.work: Schuster, Sacramentary III, Twenty-first Sunday, printed pp. 178–181
source_checks.lines: 11125–11340 plus independently rendered retained excerpt images for printed pp. 178 and 181
source_checks.outcome: Innocent Job as Christ’s figure, family/practical virtue, twofold Secret effect, present deprivation of light, and inward sacramental fruit are supported. Christ bears others’ sin; the literal innocent Job is not converted into the Gospel’s guilty servant. Schuster’s present judgment remains distinct from Augustine’s final judgment.

chronology_lookups.lookup: Composition; story at Susa, writing-place uncertain; B.C. 465–425, conjectural early dating/later date possible.
chronology_lookups.source: CE V (1909), Esther, line 17 authorship/date paragraph and following later-date discussion; DR Esth. 1:2 and 2:5.
chronology_lookups.outcome: Date is a qualified book-composition estimate, not the prayer’s utterance or Greek addition’s independent date. Susa is the story place. Correctly scoped.

chronology_lookups.lookup: Composition of Job; story in Hus (Uz), writing-place unknown; probably seventh–fifth centuries B.C.
chronology_lookups.source: USCCB Job introduction, https://bible.usccb.org/bible/job/0; DR Job 1:1 and the appointed composite.
chronology_lookups.outcome: Probable composition span is not a year for Job’s suffering. Composite keeps both stages of permission recognizable. Correctly scoped.

chronology_lookups.lookup: Historical setting; occasion/site unknown; occasion date unresolved.
chronology_lookups.source: Psalm passages and the study’s Psalm qualification; Augustine NPNF Ps. 90 §2 and Ps. 119 octonaries.
chronology_lookups.outcome: Shared unresolved answer does not manufacture a common occasion. Correctly scoped.

chronology_lookups.passage: Shared Introit, Gradual, Alleluia Ps. 113:1, Communion
chronology_lookups.lookup: Psalms composition; collection-wide bound, individual places unknown; before c. 165 B.C.

chronology_lookups.outcome: The bound is explicit as collection-wide and does not assign one individual date to all four liturgical uses. Correctly scoped.

chronology_lookups.lookup: Retrospective Exodus event; departure from Egypt, interval ending at Jerusalem’s Temple; preferred 480th year (Vulgate), alternative 440th (Septuagint).
chronology_lookups.source: CE III (1908), Biblical Chronology, lines 153–157, especially Temple interval paragraph.
chronology_lookups.outcome: Both endpoints and competing transmitted intervals remain visible. No absolute Exodus year or Psalm composition year inferred. Correctly scoped.

chronology_lookups.lookup: Traditional attribution to David’s reign; Psalm setting unknown; disputed B.C. 1055–1015.
chronology_lookups.source: Haydock, printed p. 781 (retained PDF excerpt 817), independently rendered/read; CE IV (1908), David, line 3.
chronology_lookups.outcome: The reign is conditional author-era orientation. Haydock distinguishes David instructing young Solomon, David himself young under Saul, and Daniel consoling captives; it still reports general Davidic attribution. The table does not treat Solomon as author or the reign as a secure Psalm occasion.

chronology_lookups.lookup: Jesus teaches in Galilee; precise venue unknown; date unresolved.
chronology_lookups.outcome: Narrative bounds support Galilee without fixing a room, day, or year. Date belongs to delivery, not composition.

chronology_lookups.lookup: Writing-place uncertain; some estimates concern a Semitic original; six disputed historical proposals c. A.D. 38–45,40–42,40–45,60–68,64–67,50.
chronology_lookups.source: CE X (1911), St. Matthew, lines 201–203; CE XIV (1912), New Testament, line 29.
chronology_lookups.outcome: Alternatives preserved without averaging or claiming current consensus or one date of the extant Greek Gospel. Minor appendix page-range issue only: SYN-001.

chronology_lookups.lookup: Composition in captivity; Rome favored, Caesarea possible; readers in Asia Minor; disputed A.D. 58–63 and A.D. 61.
chronology_lookups.source: CE V (1909), Epistle to the Ephesians, readers and date/place paragraphs (line 69); CE XI (1911), St. Paul, line 45; Eph. 6:20.
chronology_lookups.outcome: Writer’s possible locations are distinguished from readers and military imagery. Competing dates are not two episodes. Correctly scoped.

visual_inspection.method: tools/pdf-review in dedicated replaceable children, then actual full-page image inspection of each of ten concise pages and three source excerpts. Contact sheet alone was not used to assert inspection.

pages.outcome: All seventeen appointed entries in order, including conditional mission and Luke additions, Trinity Preface and Credo note; branch rules readable; exactly four sense overview rows.

The sole Scriptural Date and Location dossier occupies one page. Three columns permit passage→occurrence/place/date lookup. Nine rows, shared answers and qualifications are readable; no long detailed annotation stuffed into a narrow cell.
Substantive themes: family receives before acting; freedom meets brother and battle. Readable paragraphs and notes; no padding.
Substantive themes: wounded still belong to their helper; food bears its destination. Completes the two-page movement with normal breathing room.
Developed commentary begins here. Debt, gifts, Augustine and Chrysostom reason together within the question; clear footnotes.
Aquinas’s qualification and Job’s counterexample deepen the argument beyond the opening; coherent page flow and note area.
Armor/protection and competing glosses are readable; explanations remain interleaved rather than separate author capsules.
Food, inward fruit and judgment develop distinct reasoning; dense but comfortable house typography and readable notes.
Judgment discussion finishes, then scope begins. No collision, clipping, stranded heading or unexplained abbreviation.
References and generation colophon finish the ten-page document. Remaining space is ordinary terminal matter, not length padding.

limits: Review covers this concise derivation against the accepted full-study argument and exact adopted source loci; it is not an exhaustive search of patristic or modern scholarship.

Schuster and Haydock retained page excerpts were newly rendered and read, but their entire large source scans were not rehashed in this stage.

Direct USCCB opens returned 403; official-site search results successfully returned the relevant Job composition statement and Psalms dating paragraph. No claim of reading a successful live full-page response is made.

The general-calendar mission/Luke conditions and text distinctions were compared to the full study; this stage did not supply a new local-calendar ruling or repeat the full foundational text/rights audit.

No blocking defect found. SYN-001 is a minor overbroad appendix locator.
